title: Blood DNA Extraction Protocol for T. cruzi Detection via LAMP-PCR
author: Sneider Gutierrez
materials: Equipment · Vortex mixer Centrifuge (capable of 12,000 × g) Heater (prewarmed to 70 °C) Timer
Cold Storage · A bucket with ice

Reagents & Buffers CTAB 2% lysis buffer (CTAB: 2% (w/v), Tris-HCl (pH 8.0): 100 mM, EDTA: 20 mM, NaCl: 1.4 M. 5 M NaCl (cold/onice) Isopropanol (cold/onice) 70% ethanol PCR-grade nuclease-free water (incubate at 70 °C)
1 min on ice to improve protein precipitation

Reagents & Buffers CTAB 2% lysis buffer (CTAB: 2% (w/v), Tris-HCl (pH 8.0): 100 mM, EDTA: 20 mM, NaCl: 1.4 M. 5 M NaCl (cold/onice) Isopropanol (cold/onice) 70% ethanol PCR-grade nuclease-free water (incubate at 70 °C)

steps.title: Label tubes
steps.instruction: Label each 2 mL tube on the left side with date and operator’s initials, on the top with sample order and “NA”, and leave the right side blank for future DNA concentration values.

steps.title: Decontaminate gloves
steps.instruction: Dampen a paper towel with 10 % bleach and wipe gloves between each sample to prevent cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Add whole blood
steps.instruction: Add 300 mL of fresh whole blood collected in EDTA to a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube (do not use low‑binding tubes).

steps.title: Lyse cells with CTAB
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of CTAB lysis buffer to the blood, mix, and incubate at 65 °C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Add NaCl and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Pipette 500 µL of 5 M NaCl into the lysed sample three times, then centrifuge at 12 000 × g for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully pipette 1 mL of the clear supernatant from top to bottom without touching the pellet and transfer it to a new, pre‑labeled 2 mL tube.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of cold isopropanol to the transferred supernatant, invert the tube gently 20 times (palms sandwich technique) to mix, then centrifuge at 12 000 × g for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Optional low‑temperature incubation
steps.instruction: If no visible precipitation occurs, incubate the tube on ice or at –20 °C for 10 minutes before proceeding.

steps.title: Remove isopropanol supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully pipette off the supernatant without disturbing the DNA pellet; discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Wash pellet with 70 % ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of 70 % ethanol to the pellet, invert gently, then centrifuge at 12 000 × g for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Discard ethanol and dry pellet
steps.instruction: Invert the tube upside‑down once, tap repeatedly on a paper towel while gently rotating to drain ethanol, then dry the pellet at 70 °C for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Resuspend dried pellet
steps.instruction: Add 25–50 µL of pre‑heated buffer (25–50 µL) to the dried pellet, pipette up and down 20 times, then incubate at 70 °C for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Vortex and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Vortex the resuspended DNA for 5 seconds, then centrifuge at 12 000 × g for 1 minute.

steps.title: Quantify DNA
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration using a NanoDrop, taking the sample from the top of the solution.

steps.title: Optional 100 % ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of 100 % ethanol to the pellet, invert gently, then discard the ethanol by inverting and tapping the tube as described earlier.

steps.title: Store extracted DNA
steps.instruction: Store the resuspended DNA at 4 °C for short‑term use (up to 1 week).

steps.title: Prepare LAMP master mix
steps.instruction: Retrieve the LAMP‑PCR master mix from –20 °C, spin it down, and ensure inclusion of a negative and a positive control; verify sufficient vials are available.

steps.title: Thaw SYBR Green
steps.instruction: Thaw the SYBR Green solution at 4 °C before use.

steps.title: Add SYBR Green to lid
steps.instruction: Add 2 µL of SYBR Green to the lid of the LAMP reaction tube.

steps.title: Spin down and record color
steps.instruction: Spin the tube briefly and record the result: brown indicates a negative reaction, green indicates a positive reaction.

steps.title: Incubate LAMP reaction
steps.instruction: Incubate the LAMP reaction at 65 °C for 1 hour.

steps.title: Add template DNA
steps.instruction: Load 5 µL of the pre‑extracted DNA into the LAMP reaction and pipette the mixture 5 times to ensure homogeneity.
